title: Grateful Dead Live at Meramec Community College on 1970-05-14
lineage: SBD > MR > ? > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑voltage 1970 show, highlighted by a scorching Lovelight and the New Speedway→Nobody’s Fault jam.
ai_review.review: The recording is a solid soundboard source that, while a bit rough around the edges by modern standards, remains clear and highly listenable for its era. Musically the concert shines with a blistering New Speedway‑NFA‑Lovelight sequence, fire‑brand performances of Schoolgirl, St. Stephen and the first-ever Attics, plus an acoustic set that many fans cite as “sweet.” Overall the energy is high‑octane and the pacing tight, making it one of the standout 1970 dates.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews overwhelmingly praise the performance and note good‑to‑excellent soundboard quality; only a single mixed review tempers the average, yielding an overall rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear for a 1970 soundboard; a few reviewers call it "a little rough" or note occasional low levels in the acoustic set, but overall it is listenable and better than many contemporary tapes.

standout_songs: New Speedway → Nobody's Fault → New Speedway jam
show_quality.setlist_flow: The show opens with a sweet acoustic set (Silver Threads, etc.) that leads into an electric half‑hour of nonstop energy—New Speedway, the NFA sandwich and a breakneck Lovelight—all tied together by fiery Pigpen harmonica and Jerry’s snarling guitar. The pacing keeps the momentum high from start to finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his fierce guitar tone, guttural vocals and “punching you in the guts” style; a few reviewers call this performance average only by comparison to other ’70 peaks.
band_member_comments.Bob: Acoustic set noted as sweet but no specific commentary on his rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Drums: Only one drummer (Bill Kreutzmann) is mentioned; reviewers note the solid, driving drumming despite the solo lineup.
